notes.title: How we planned our Press Release campaign!
notes.content:
Running a good press release is not as easy as it might sound… Here’s our troubled experience with The Tsar's Secret!
Press releases are a good ally when trying to get our game out there. We wanted to have it highlighted to thousands of readers, of course, but also to appear on Google! Sometimes, when I overhear an indie title, it’s hard to find any website or even the Twitter account when googling it. I didn’t want this to happen with The Tsar’s Secret, so… having a bunch of journalists, bloggers, or influencers talking about it sounded like a nice solution.

To succeed (or at least try to) on your press release campaign, these were the steps we followed:

[h2]1. Build a personal database[/h2]
The point here is to research for press, journalists, bloggers, and podcasters that are more likely to write about your game. Remember that you only have a few bullets. Aim at a specific target. This way, it’s easier for people interested in your game to find it.

Some characteristics can give you a hint about the affinity of a journalist/press:

[list][*] [b]Genre[/b]: some newspapers or journalists like to cover indie games or discover hidden gems in the vast jungle of indie games. 
[*] [b]Similar games[/b]: you should reach out to journalists who’ve covered games similar to yours.
[*] [b]Geographically relevant[/b]: think if your audience is local or if your game can be of any interest to a wider audience. The US is the biggest market, so it’s always interesting. If possible, cover all the countries/languages that your game will be available.[/list]

In our case, we looked for press covering indie games and writing about stealth titles like Shadow Tactics, Serial Cleaners, and Invisible Ink among others. We didn’t focus on any country in specific, but it is funny how the international media paid more attention to our press release than the Spanish! Where’s the local pride & support?

[h2]2. Prepare the materials[/h2]
It’s time to write down that awesome news you have to share with the world!
First, think about what you want to achieve with this Press Release. What is your goal? Maybe you just want to announce your game, get more wishlists, or get more views on your new trailer. Depending on your goals, you’ll set up a certain Call To Action (CTA) on your press release. Think also about the length. Some news is longer than others, but keep it as short as possible.
Use your hook! Journalists and bloggers receive many emails a day, you have to catch their attention using the hook of your game. Probably, you already defined this for making the store descriptions. Use graphics, art, links to the trailer, etc, and optimize it for web. And build a good Press Kit!
We could not emphasize enough, double-check everything! There’s always a broken link or something wrong. Send a test mail before the real campaign.

[h2]3. Timing[/h2]
The main rule here is to pull the trigger anytime you have a newsworthy statement to make. There are many events worth covering: Playtesting, new patches, DLCs, crowdfunding campaigns, and, of course, the release. You want your game to be alive, and for that, you’ll need to create content. Try to, at least, have 1 announcement per month. 
Before a special date, unless you are Kojima or GTA, contact journalists and influencers 7 - 15 days in advance. This will give them enough time to review your Press Release.

[h2]4. Sending it![/h2]
Even as easy as “sending it!” might sound, you have to keep an eye on this step as well. Research for the best times and dates for each country. Try to avoid sending your press release when another big announcement is happening.

So… This is the theory. And we got a quite good opening rate after our launch campaign. Although, not many people wrote about our title. What worked best for us was focusing on EVEN MORE indie bloggers, contacting them through Twitter, interacting on threads, and so on. Maybe it’s because our game is still “too indie” or maybe because we just launched a demo, and not the full game. We are not Kojima, yeah…

Some Twitter accounts that helped us are: https://twitter.com/IndieBandits, https://twitter.com/IndieGamesWTF, and https://twitter.com/xblpartypodcast go and give them the love they deserve!

notes.title: The music in The Tsar's Secret
notes.content:
We truly put a lot of effort and time into it. Music is one of the pillars of The Tsar's Secret since Tenebris focuses on the sounds for creating the visual design.
In The Tsar's Secret, you are an occultist mage that can use two spells: Tenebris & Silentium. The idea is that by using Tenebris, you kind of 'erase' light from the world, so your enemies will be blind, but you will also. On the other side, Silentium will switch off sounds from reality, so you and your enemies won't be able to hear clearly.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/454c17cbdc99fb38437b55672c0cf28b3d386e20.gif[/img]
As you might notice when playing, Silentium does not wholly mute the game. You can still hear the music and SFX, but as if you were hearing it from inside a soundproof bubble. We made this decision because making a whole mode without any music is quite challenging. At first, we tried it but soon discarded the idea. Playing without music wasn't as engaging as we wanted it to be.

So, yes, music is one of the pilars of this game. We want the experience of The Tsar's Secret to be as immersive as posible. Hearing distant noises such as a fountaing, footsteps behind the walls, or the tictac of the clock help to transform the game into a truthful experience.

[h2]Creating the music[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/a98b5e38b81d62e8dc2d63f6ddf95a5337f8a181.gif[/img]
We used real imperialist russian music as the base for the theme, but adding dark and fantasy elements on top of it. In the beginning, the firsts versions of the music were more cheerful, like the main aesthetic references. But for a stealth game it felt odd.
The challenge in creating these music pieces was to keep the essence, mantaining an aesthetic coherence. But also to make it fit the genre and the situation. We needed the music to mantain the player in a tension mode during the whole level.

One of the pieces that we cherised is the music box's song. Did you noticed it? I think it's the kind of element that usally goes unnoticed!
Let us know what you think about the music and which one is your favourite song from the game.

Pst, pst!
You can discover secret passages just in Tenebris mode!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/7d10e8dc72258650941f2173f74b0b73ded15b44.gif[/img]

notes.title: Patch Note 01
notes.content:
Hi everyone!
We just uploaded a new version of the game fixing some minor bugs we found.
To let you know, players reported that the game crashes with a "fatal error" sometimes. We are still looking for this bug and trying to find a way to fix it. If this happens to you, try to close the game and open it again. That should do the trick.

[h3]— PATCH NOTES —[/h3]

- Fixed a bug that made enemies from lvl 2 disappear.
- Edited a typo in the intro.

Thanks everyone for playing, and keep sending us comments. It really helps us to improve!

notes.title: Dev. log: Creation of Grigori
notes.content:
Hi everyone!
Today we want to talk about the character creation process.
In the beginning, creating the mechanics and ensuring the fun was our main focus. Things such as narrative, characters, or historical setting were put on hold. In fact, it's mainly the Art department that took care of these topics.
The first decision made was about the general artistic direction of the game. We kind of decided it together, but the Art department had more influence on the topic. After, we started creating the main chatacter. There were some fixed concepts that Design needed to have, such as the use of occultist powers, the name of the main character, and his clothing style - influenced by the artistic direction of the game itself - but the rest came from our favourite doodling Concept Art team.

[h2]Grigori, our main character.[/h2]
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/3b8142d138ebc28562470c7ab40c7110eba26687.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/3b8142d138ebc28562470c7ab40c7110eba26687.gif[/img][/url]

He’s a double agent and an occultist mage. Cold as a stone, he leaves nothing to chance. Very dark and sexy, we know it. BUT, we have a list of traits you might not expect about him!

[i]"Mainly from his appearance, I think he's a bit of a fanatic for his looks. Always sweeping his hair back and glancing at himself in a reflection. Maybe a bit vain".[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/b1240fbe12bad476871fdc9dbd8f59683ba5cc24.jpg[/img]

I asked Miki what she imagined about Grigori when creating the concept art for the character. These are the sentences she wrote back to me.
[i]"Grigori strikes me as the kind to get very tense about things and cover it up with drinking or some kind of activity. And something that I thought of for him is maybe he's artistic in some aspect. Poetry, painting, music, perhaps gardening".[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/b8128df0b06e7e47d01747d5cb4c898470a43d2e.jpg[/img]

Just to let you know, the whole Design team acepted that Grigori is a gardener, as a fact. So, now, our dark, misterious and cold ocultist mage is the kind that will silently judge you when you step on the grass of the Palace.

Take a look at these concepts. We were deciding the final look for Grigori. Do you like the final result?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/e40c792a511e336d7dcabaf11b76daa31149d6d7.jpg[/img]

notes.title: We are Otter Worlds Games!
notes.content:
Hello! It’s already been 4 days since the big launch of our demo on Steam. Now that I’m writing about it, publishing a demo doesn’t sound like a big milestone. But for us, as a team, it means finally being able to show all the work that we’ve been doing for 8 months.

[h2]DEVELOPER STUDIO[/h2]

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/a1973893fe4a76226ab5c797d890d13607086d18.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42657756/085aaa0fb734340063b77d19a079726a0a66ccfe.png[/img][/url]

We are Otter Worlds Games, an indie developer studio from Spain. We are scattered around the country and work remote, but sometimes we manage to meet in Madrid and have some fun together.
We started this project almost by chance, starting as a big group of: developers, programmers, artists, producers and marketers. For an indie studio, we are quite a lot of people working together and meeting every Thursday to talk about the game, what can be done, and what already has been done.

[h2]THE NAME[/h2]
When it comes to deciding important stuff, we like to involve the whole team. We started creating an excel document to vomit all the ideas we had for a cool name. Then we discovered that, not only the term "Otter" was repeated in several ideas, but they were also the most voted names among all. This is quite hilarius, how did it happened that so many Otter lovers ended together doing a videogame?

[url=https://bit.ly/3AYMJRx]Click to download Otter Worlds Sticker pack to Telegram.[/url]
[b]If you have played The Tsar's Secret, let us know what you think about the game![/b]

Fun fact about us: we have a Meme department.
